<issue>
LRU cache __wrapped__ attribute returns None instead of wrapped function

#### Description

When accessing the `__wrapped__` attribute on a function decorated with `@functools.lru_cache`, astroid incorrectly returns `None` instead of the original wrapped function.

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce

```python
import functools
import astroid

code = '''
import functools

class Foo(object):
    @functools.lru_cache()
    def foo(self):
        pass

f = Foo()
f.foo.__wrapped__
'''

module = astroid.parse(code)
wrapped_attr = list(module.body[-1].value.infer())[0]
print(f"Expected: FunctionDef, Got: {type(wrapped_attr)}")
```

The `__wrapped__` attribute should return the original function that was decorated, but instead it returns `None`. This breaks code analysis tools that rely on being able to access the wrapped function through this standard attribute.
</issue>
